evals.prompt: I do not have the quotation software on this computer. Create an import-ready USD quotation JSON for two PX-100 pumps at USD 1200 each, manual selling price USD 1500, customer Acme Marine, quotation Q-2026-101. Do not make PDF.
evals.expected_output: A validated schema-v3 quotation JSON is delivered without requiring or attempting to use Quotation Software.
expectations: The final quotation JSON passes the bundled validator.
The JSON contains the requested customer, quotation number, quantity, currency, and manual unit selling price.
Missing software does not prevent JSON delivery and no PDF success is claimed.

evals.prompt: Make quotation Q-2026-102 and a pending compact goods receipt for one received pump. I also want both PDFs, but this is my first time using the skill and I have not told you where the portable app is.
evals.expected_output: The skill creates and validates the quotation JSON with a pending goods-receipt draft first, asks for the portable .exe path, and does not fabricate PDFs while configuration is missing.
expectations: A valid JSON containing pendingGoodsReceiptDraft is produced before PDF setup is resolved.
The user is asked for the portable Quotation Software executable path or may decline setup.
The response clearly identifies PDF as pending rather than replacing the renderer or claiming success.

evals.prompt: Using my configured quotation software, create quotation and goods-receipt PDFs from a complete bilingual-capable quotation JSON. Use the latest published exchange rates and give me the JSON, both PDFs, and the export result.
evals.expected_output: The JSON validates independently. A compatible configured portable app exports both PDFs with refresh enabled and records exact rates; an older incompatible app leaves the JSON intact and PDF output pending.
expectations: The quotation JSON passes validation before PDF export starts.
PDFs are produced only by a schema-compatible configured Quotation Software executable; incompatibility is reported without dropping history or claiming PDF success.
The export result records exchangeRateDate and the exact applied exchangeRates.

evals.prompt: Create an import-ready quotation using the spreadsheet template. If my quotation editor is already open, import it through the current programmatic API and validate it for quotation PDF export.
evals.expected_output: The generated schema-v3 JSON preserves templateId spreadsheet, passes offline validation, and uses quotationAgentV2 with export preflight when an open editor is available.
expectations: The final JSON contains quotation.templateId set to spreadsheet rather than classic.
The bundled validator passes the final file.
Open-editor automation awaits quotationAgentReady and prefers quotationAgentV2 over UI simulation or the legacy API.

evals.prompt: Update the working quotation validity to 60 days. Keep all existing saved revisions unchanged; do not create a new revision. I only need JSON.
evals.expected_output: A valid schema-v3 JSON with changed working validity and byte-equivalent saved revision data.
expectations: The complete envelope passes offline validation.
The family ID, archive IDs, archive snapshots, and working revision number are unchanged.
Only the working quotation validity changes; no application is required.

evals.prompt: Create the next revision from this quotation, then add a new row for two valves at USD 45 cost each. Keep the previous offer in history. JSON only.
evals.expected_output: The current working revision is frozen before adding the new row to the next working revision.
expectations: All earlier saved snapshots remain unchanged.
The newly saved snapshot contains the pre-edit working quotation without the valves.
The next working revision increments once and includes the requested new row with a unique ID.

evals.prompt: Restore saved revision 1 as a new working revision. Keep completed goods receipts. Return an updated JSON without using the app.
evals.expected_output: Current work is archived, revision 1 is copied into the next numbered draft, completed receipts remain, and the pending receipt is cleared.
expectations: The output passes offline validation.
Existing archives are unchanged and the former working quotation is archived.
The family ID and current completed goods-receipt records are retained; pendingGoodsReceiptDraft is absent from the new working quotation.

evals.prompt: Delete saved revision 1 from this quotation. Keep the working draft and other revision numbers as they are. Write a separate output JSON.
evals.expected_output: Only the selected archive is removed, with no renumbering or loss of working data.
expectations: The source file is unchanged and the output validates.
Saved revision 2 retains its original ID, number, and contents.
Working revision 3 and its commercial data remain unchanged.

evals.prompt: Render this quotation with history using my configured app. Its api-info reports API 2.0.0 and quotationSchemaVersion 2. Do not change any quotation data.
evals.expected_output: The skill retains validated schema-v3 JSON and reports the app compatibility blocker without removing history or claiming a PDF.
expectations: No schema downgrade or history stripping occurs.
The old app is not used to render the unsupported file.
The response identifies a compatible portable build as needed; it does not rebuild or change configuration without that work being requested.
